statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because CME equity index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress holds in the high band on a 5.18% 10-year yield at its highest since 2007, WTI near $92 with the Strait of Hormuz still disrupted, and a rejected Iranian reopening proposal that leaves the weekend unpriced into the 22:00Z restart.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise behind part of Friday's oil decline would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this publication.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures shut, while a rejected Hormuz plan, fresh Saudi-Yemen strikes and a 5.18% 10-year yield hold Stress high into the 22:00Z restart
body:
Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects an absent path rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.86 prior close, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 after a 15.94 session high. Contemporaneous reporting has the S&P 500 up 0.51% at 7,743.41, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.48% at 27,068.72 and the Dow up 0.93% at 51,828.62. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent.

Stress stays in the high band for three independent reasons. Rates are the structural pressure: H.15 puts the 10-year at 5.18% and the 2-year at 4.87%, with the 10-year at its highest level since 2007 and record AI-linked corporate issuance competing for the same capital. Energy is the second: WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33% on Friday specifically on optimism that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen, and that premise was withdrawn on Saturday when the Iranian seven-day proposal was publicly rejected, with Tehran stating it still awaits a definitive reply. The third is a widening regional escalation: Saudi-led forces reported intercepting Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and the Yanbu Aramco facility, then struck Taiz in western Yemen, which contests Red Sea export capacity while Hormuz is already disrupted.

The important distinction is that none of this is yet a price path. Under this contract event importance, diplomatic reversal and surprise magnitude inform Stress and Confidence until observed market structure supports Tail, so the mapped state stays EA_ON and the protection is expressed as a narrow danger window across the 22:00Z restart rather than a broad shutdown. Cross-asset internals also argue against alignment: on the latest session 6 of 8 megacaps rose but dispersion was 1.92%, with MSFT up 3.66% against META down 3.33%, and 6 of 7 semiconductors rose with QCOM up 3.97% against INTC down 3.45%. That is rotation, not the uniform one-way alignment that would amplify Tail. Federal funding is not a near-term catalyst, since the continuing resolution passed on 1 September funds the government through 11 December. Confidence is set at 75: verified index, volatility, yield, crude and calendar evidence is complete, but there is no live price path during the weekend halt, the shared Finviz futures and calendar sections were unavailable this cycle, and two sources disagreed on the Brent level, so no Brent figure is published here.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were carried forward unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 6-8 range, Stress rose from 49 to 66 and Confidence decayed from 82 to 75 across the period, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, energy and geopolitical backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON with dominant mode normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours, so the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, then lifts from roughly 18:00Z into the published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where the rejected Hormuz proposal and the Saudi-Yemen exchange meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. Conditional Tail peaks at 17 in the first full hour after the restart, then decays through the Asian session as liquidity normalises, easing to single digits by the European open. A modest lift to 9 is carried across the 13:30Z US cash open, where opening-auction continuation without a shallow pullback would be the first genuine Tail evidence of the week. Every forecast hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not an assertion that future structure has been observed.

forecastDetail.comment: Futures remain shut since Friday 21:00Z, so the low Tail reflects an absent price path rather than an observed benign trend; Friday's orderly mid-range close and a 14.87 VIX supply no mean-reversion-failure amplifier.

Tail holds at the closed-period baseline while Stress stays high, because Saturday's rejection of Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan withdraws the premise behind part of Friday's 2.33% WTI decline and cannot be priced until 22:00Z.

Tail edges up on restart proximity alone. Iran's stated wait for a definitive US reply is the main conditional discontinuity, and such a headline would arrive into the thinnest liquidity of the week.
